questions.explain: The chapter explains that this separation lets you describe what you want without specifying how, which is what enables a well-tuned relational engine to serve billions of rows to millions of users predictably.
options: It lets DBAs avoid learning query syntax
It removes the need for indexes entirely
It guarantees that all queries run in constant time
It allows a well-tuned engine to serve billions of rows with predictable behavior
questions.q: According to the chapter, what is the key reason the separation of query intent from execution strategy matters in relational databases?

questions.explain: The chapter's session-query example uses sys.dm_exec_sessions joined to sys.dm_exec_requests and calls them the pulse monitors you will return to constantly.
questions.q: Which pair of DMVs does the chapter describe as the "pulse monitors" of a running SQL Server instance — who is connected, what each session is running, and what it is waiting on?

questions.explain: The chapter states performance investigation — e.g. a query jumping from 200 ms to 45 seconds — consumes more DBA time than any other activity.
questions.q: In the chapter's breakdown of what DBAs actually do in production, which activity consumes more DBA time than any other?

questions.explain: The mindset section lists "they measure before they optimize" as a core habit, warning that assumptions about root causes are usually wrong.
options: Always raise isolation levels to Serializable
Measure before optimizing, reaching for monitoring data and wait statistics before making changes
Document decisions only when an outage occurs
questions.q: Which of the following is listed in the chapter as a habit of high-impact DBAs?
